questions.q: What is the primary physical setting of the poem "?kj dh ;kn" and what time period does it suggest?
questions.a: The primary setting is an old ancestral house (described through cracked walls, leaky roof, broken windows, and multiple generations living together) suggesting a timeless, possibly pre-modern Indian joint family home. A wrong answer that only says "a house" or "village" reveals the student hasn't noticed the specific sensory details (e.g., "izk.k eu f?kjrk", "pkj HkkbZ pkj cfgusa") that establish both the physical decay and the historical depth of the setting.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the poet creates a sense of nostalgia through the description of the house's deterioration.
questions.a: The poet juxtaposes physical decay (cracked walls, leaking roof) with intimate family moments (father's chair, mother's kitchen, children playing) so that each flaw in the house becomes a vessel for memory — the broken window isn't just damage, it's where father sat; the leaking roof isn't just a problem, it's where monsoon memories live. A wrong answer that treats decay and nostalgia as separate ideas shows the student misses the poem's central technique: the setting's flaws are precisely what make it emotionally rich.

questions.q: In stanza 3 (beginning "vkt xhrk ikB djosQ"), the poet describes future visitors reacting to the house. Apply the concept of atmosphere to explain what mood this imagined future scene creates for the present reader.
questions.a: The imagined future visitors ("[ksyrs ;k [kM+s gksaxs") who will find the house strange and ask its name creates a poignant atmosphere of impermanence and loss — it makes the reader feel the fragility of the poet's world, knowing this living memory will become a ruin. Steps: 1) Identify the future scene described. 2) Note the contrast between current intimate knowledge ("ik¡posa dk uke") and future ignorance. 3) Recognize this projection forward deepens the present atmosphere of bittersweet attachment. A wrong answer focusing only on the visitors' actions misses the emotional effect on the reader.

questions.q: Analyze how the repetition of "?kj u”kj esa frj jgk gS" (the house stands in the courtyard) at the end of multiple stanzas functions structurally to reinforce both setting and atmosphere.
questions.a: The refrain acts as an anchor — each time it returns, it pulls the reader back to the physical reality of the house (setting) while accumulating emotional weight (atmosphere) because the preceding stanzas have added new memories to that same location. The house becomes a fixed point around which time, memory, and decay swirl. A wrong answer that calls it "just a chorus" or "repetition for rhythm" fails to see how the refrain structurally binds the poem's physical and emotional dimensions.

questions.q: Evaluate whether the poem's atmosphere is ultimately one of despair or resilience. Support your judgment with two specific textual evidences.
questions.a: The atmosphere is resilience — despite overwhelming physical decay ("jkr Hkj fxjrk", "izk.k eu f?kjrk"), the poem ends with the speaker claiming ownership of the house's story ("dke djrk gw¡ fd dguk / uke djrk gw¡ fd dguk") and asserting "eSa e”ks esa gw¡ lgh gS". Evidence 1: The father's voice persists in memory ("firk th dgrs jgs gSa") showing continuity. Evidence 2: The final stanza transforms the house from a decaying object into a living narrative the poet controls. A wrong answer choosing "despair" ignores the poet's agency in the closing lines and the warmth that permeates the decay.

questions.q: Write a four-line stanza in Hindi that uses a specific setting detail (like a broken swing, a faded photograph, a silent courtyard) to create an atmosphere of bittersweet memory, modeling the technique used in "?kj dh ;kn".
questions.a: A strong answer will: 1) Choose one concrete setting detail. 2) Attach a specific memory to it. 3) Use sensory language (smell, sound, touch). 4) End with an emotional resonance that lingers. Example: "tutte jhule ki vo jhankaar / ab bhi sunti hai raat bhar / nanhi ungliyon ki woh mehak / khamosh aangan mein bas rahi". A poor answer uses abstract nouns ("sadness", "memory") without a physical anchor, showing the student hasn't grasped how the poem makes atmosphere through concrete setting.
